transformations.edit: Adapted the inherent `[u8]` receiver to an explicit `slice: &[u8]` parameter and named return for Verus; the executable target body preserves the initial unequal-length return, the SSE2 chunk dispatch, and the simple-helper fallback.

Specialized the source `#[cfg(all(target_arch = "x86_64", target_feature = "sse2"))]` block to the active verification target, whose rustc cfg reports `target_arch="x86_64"` and `target_feature="sse2"`; the block's `CHUNK_SIZE = 16`, length guard, and early return are preserved.

Instantiated the generated shared ASCII vocabulary with the frozen source-backed definitions of `ascii_is_uppercase`, `ascii_lower_byte`, and `ascii_eq_ignore_case`; added `#![auto]` only as a Verus quantifier-trigger annotation.

Declared `eq_ignore_ascii_case_simple` as a narrowly named private-helper boundary with the source-backed postcondition `ret <==> ascii_eq_ignore_case(slice@, other@)` under the equal-length precondition required by the target body; the target body itself is not external.

Declared `eq_ignore_ascii_case_chunks::<N>` as a narrowly named private-helper boundary with the same source-backed postcondition under the source invariants `N > 0`, equal lengths, and `slice.len() >= N`; this boundary includes the helper-local `eq_ignore_ascii_inner` and tail logic rather than the target body.
Added proof-only assertions that the unequal-length early return falsifies `ascii_eq_ignore_case`; this has no executable control-flow or data-flow effect.
